sections.label: D
sections.title: Check the correct answer.
sections.note: Use too after an affirmative statement and either after a negative statement.

questions.prompt: 1. Thomas Edison was an inventor. Alexander Graham Bell was, ___.
questions.explanation: Both statements are affirmative, so use too.

questions.prompt: 2. The hardware store sells hammers. It sells nails, ___.
questions.explanation: Both statements are affirmative, so use too.

questions.prompt: 3. This computer isn't difficult to use. The DVD player isn't, ___.
questions.explanation: Both statements are negative, so use either.

questions.prompt: 4. I don't have homework tonight. My brother doesn't, ___.
questions.explanation: Both statements are negative, so use either.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Use too or either.
sections.note: Read whether each pair of statements is affirmative or negative.

questions.prompt: 1. This lamp doesn't have a light bulb. The closet lamp doesn't, ___.
questions.explanation: The two statements are negative, so use either.

questions.prompt: 2. Jessica loves the seesaw. Mimi loves it, ___.
questions.explanation: The two statements are affirmative, so use too.

questions.prompt: 3. Mitsuko has a red bicycle. Kim has a red bicycle, ___.
questions.explanation: The two statements are affirmative, so use too.

parts.label: Correct picture word

sections.label: J
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose a comparative form for two people and a superlative form for one person in a whole group.

questions.prompt: 1. This glassblower works ___ the other one.
questions.explanation: Two glassblowers are being compared, so use the comparative form more cheerfully than.

questions.prompt: 2. Nancy works ___ Caroline.
questions.explanation: Nancy and Caroline are two people, so use the comparative form more quietly than.

questions.prompt: 3. Sachiko works ___ of all the students.
questions.explanation: Of all the students requires the superlative form the hardest.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use the best phrase from the box. One phrase is not needed.

questions.prompt: 1. Harriet ice skates ___.
questions.explanation: Harriet is compared with the whole group, so use the most beautifully.

questions.prompt: 2. Zack lifts the chair ___ than Joe.
questions.explanation: The picture compares how easily Zack and Joe lift a chair, so use more easily.

questions.prompt: 3. Ken rides ___.
questions.explanation: Ken is ahead of the whole group, so use the fastest.

questions.prompt: 4. Janette blows glass ___ than Andrea.
questions.explanation: The picture compares Janette with Andrea, so use more skillfully than.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Combine the sentences using comparative or superlative adverbs.
sections.note: Use the word in parentheses and keep the original meaning.

questions.prompt: 1. Jana can jump 1 meter. Nina can jump 1.5 meters. (high)
answers: Nina can jump higher than Jana
questions.explanation: Nina reaches a greater height, so Nina jumps higher than Jana.

questions.prompt: 2. Nick arrived at 3:15. The other students arrived at 3:00. (late)
answers: Nick arrived later than the other students
Nick arrived later than the other students.
questions.explanation: 3:15 is later than 3:00, so Nick arrived later than the other students.

questions.prompt: 3. Violet finished her homework in five minutes. Yolanda finished her homework in ten minutes. (quickly)
answers: Violet finished her homework more quickly than Yolanda
Violet finished her homework more quickly than Yolanda.
questions.explanation: Five minutes is less time than ten minutes, so Violet finished more quickly than Yolanda.
